newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds shrug off rate rise talk, move up.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds shrug off rate rise talk, move up.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds shrugged off talk of a possible rate rise in the Netherlands and of a variable repo rate in Germany to move higher in active business on Wednesday, although traders spoke of a "toppy" feeling.
"For me the market is feeling a bit toppish at the moment. We could see a small correction," one trader said.
Others spoke of a mood of caution shadowing the market.

Traders said that while the growing speculation of a small rate rise in the Netherlands and a de facto rise in Germany if a variable repo rate is introduced had not fazed the market on Wednesday, it was still a factor to be taken into consideration.

Traders noted that money market rates had started to decline after days of rallying as the Belgian central bank, which has been keeping liquidity tight to protect the franc, had finally eased liquidity a bit on Wednesday.
The one-week repo rate ended Wednesday at 3.90/3.99 percent, well down from Tuesday's 4.07/4.14 but still way above the bank's central rate of 3.00 percent.

Traders expressed frustration at the bank's refusal to explain why it had kept draining liquidity, but added that if the talk of the Dutch rate rise proved to be accurate it could provide some explanation.
The bond market is also keeping a weather eye on the flood of U.S. statistics to be released on Thursday and Friday.
Key among these are Friday's publication of data including non-farm payrolls, personal spending, factory orders and the National Association of Purchasing Managers index.
Another influence would be new bond supply coming on stream.
"There was supply yesterday and more coming, so the market will tend to stay a bit soft," one trader said.
The benchmark 10-year OLO ended Wednesday yielding 5.59 percent against 5.63 late on Tuesday, and the spread over Bunds was static at 10 basis points having widened to 12 at one stage.
They said that market makers were the main players in Belgian bonds on Wednesday, with good bidding in five and seven year paper and some selling of the 10 year maturities.
"It has been market makers today. We have been really quite busy," one trader said.
There was also a return of interest in the longer maturities, neglected in recent days due to the general focus on very short paper.
Traders noted that the move higher had been an echo of the rises in Germany and the United States, although they noted that Belgian bonds tended to lag the German ascent.
The front month futures contract was 32 basis points higher at 122.18.
